slug: 穿越大乾从病秧子开始蜕变
lines: 北境荒原，朔风如刀，卷起漫天黄沙，裹挟着浓重的血腥味。
大地已被染成暗红色，断箭残戈斜插在堆积如山的尸体上。
残破不堪的“镇北军”战旗在风中猎猎作响，旗面上满是刀剑撕裂的痕迹和凝固的血块。
“守住阵线！哪怕死也要给我守住！”
方老将军喉咙沙哑地嘶吼着，手中长枪如龙，将三名蛮族士兵同时挑飞。
他银甲尽裂，左肩深可见骨的伤口不断渗血，胸前还插着三支羽箭，却仍如山岳般屹立在阵前。
“父亲，右翼已破！蛮族重骑兵已冲破我军的防线。”
次子方文渊策马奔来，头盔已不知去向，脸上带着一道从额头到下巴的狰狞伤口，鲜血直流模糊了他的左眼。
方震天心头一紧：“你大哥呢？”
方文渊声音沙哑，抹了一把脸上的鲜血。
“大哥他...亲率铁卫冲入敌阵，以身为饵，引敌军深入雷火区，与两千蛮族精锐同归于尽了...”
方震天身形一晃，长枪深深插入地面才稳住身体。长子方文瀚，是他最骄傲的继承人，年仅四十便已统领北境三分之二的兵力，本是他方家未来的希望。
“阿爷，东面又有敌军增援！”
少年方云霆纵马而来，银甲染血，长剑已有多处缺口。
他是方家第三代中最出色的子弟，年仅十九，却已在战场上磨砺了三年。
方震天看着眼前伤痕累累的孙儿，又望向四周越来越少的镇北军、心如刀绞。
“云霆，你带着剩余士兵后撤三十里，去与中军汇合！”方震天沉声道，声音中带着不容置疑的决绝。
少年倔强地摇头：“方家的儿郎，只有战死，没有逃兵！”
“糊涂！”方震天怒吼，“你若战死，方家血脉就真的断了！京都还有你祖母和你三叔留下的铭儿、还需要你照料。”
提到那个自出生就体弱多病、被世人嘲为“方家病秧子”的方云逸，三人心中皆是一痛。
那是方家老三唯一的孩子，也是方家这一代血脉中最为脆弱的一个。
“轰隆隆——”
地面突然剧烈震动，蛮族大军中分出一条通道，十余头披着铁甲的巨象缓缓走出，象背上架着巨型弓弩。
“铁甲战象，他们竟然动用王庭禁军！”有士兵惊恐大叫。
方震天脸色剧变，知道全线溃败已不可避免。铁甲战象是蛮族王庭的象征，它们的出现意味着蛮族已倾尽全力。
“父亲，您带云霆走，我来断后！”方文渊忽然平静下来，眼中闪过决然之色。
他摘下胸前一枚青铜虎符，塞到方震天手中，“将这交给母亲，告诉她，儿子不孝，不能再侍奉她左右了。”
“文渊，不可！”方震天刚欲阻止，方文渊已调转马头，高举手中长剑。
“镇北军，随我冲锋！”
残余的士兵如同回光返照，跟随着方文渊冲向铁甲战象组成的铜墙铁壁。
方文渊一马当先，长剑在阳光下闪耀，他的身影在冲锋中显得格外孤独而壮烈。
“二叔！”方云霆嘶声痛哭，想要立刻追击上去，却被方震天死死拉住。
“走！不要让他们的战死白费！”方震天老泪纵横，强忍悲痛拉着他向后撤退。
然而，似乎为时已晚，蛮族骑兵已从两翼包抄，切断了所有退路。铁甲战象喷吐着烈焰，将残余的镇北军困在火海之中。
方震天知道逃生无望，挺起长枪，对方云霆惨然一笑：“孩子，你怕吗？”
content_en:
In the northern wilderness, the fresh wind is like a knife, rolling up yellow sand all over the sky, carrying a strong smell of blood.
The ground has been dyed dark red, and broken arrows and broken weapons are stuck diagonally on the piles of corpses.
The dilapidated battle flag of the "Zhenbei Army" rustled in the wind, and the flag was covered with marks of sword tears and coagulated blood clots.
"Hold the front! Even if you die, you must hold it for me!"
General Fang roared hoarsely, and with a spear like a dragon in his hand, he knocked three barbarian soldiers away at the same time.
His silver armor was cracked, the bone-deep wound on his left shoulder was oozing blood, and there were three feather arrows stuck in his chest, but he still stood in front of the battle like a mountain.
"Father, the right wing has been broken! The barbarian heavy cavalry has broken through our defense line."
The second son, Fang Wenyuan, galloped over with his helmet missing. There was a hideous wound on his face from his forehead to his chin, and his left eye was blurred by blood.
Fang Zhentian's heart tightened: "Where is your elder brother?"
Fang Wenyuan's voice was hoarse and he wiped the blood on his face.
"Big brother... he personally led the iron guards into the enemy's formation, used his body as bait to lure the enemy troops deep into the Thunder Fire Zone, and perished together with two thousand elite barbarians..."
Fang Zhentian's body swayed, and his spear was deeply inserted into the ground before he stabilized his body. The eldest son, Fang Wenhan, was his proudest heir. At only forty years old, he already commanded two-thirds of the troops in the northern border. He was originally the hope of his family's future.
"Grandpa, there are enemy reinforcements from the east!"
The young man Fang Yunting came on horseback, his silver armor stained with blood and his long sword with many gaps.
He is the most outstanding son of the third generation of the Fang family. He is only nineteen years old, but he has been honing his skills on the battlefield for three years.
Fang Zhentian looked at his scarred grandson in front of him, and then at the dwindling Zhenbei Army around him, with his heart pounding.
"Yunting, take the remaining soldiers and retreat thirty miles to join the Chinese army!" Fang Zhentian said solemnly, with unquestionable determination in his voice.
The young man shook his head stubbornly: "The sons of the Fang family can only die in battle, and there is no desertion!"
"Confused!" Fang Zhentian roared, "If you die in the battle, the Fang family's bloodline will really be cut off! There are still Ming'er left by your grandmother and your third uncle in Kyoto, and they still need your care."
When mentioning Fang Yunyi, who had been frail and sick since birth and was ridiculed as "the sick son of the Fang family" by the world, all three of them felt pain in their hearts.
That was the only child of the third eldest son of the Fang family, and also the most vulnerable one in this generation of the Fang family.
"Rumble--"
The ground suddenly shook violently, and a passage opened in the barbarian army. More than a dozen giant elephants wearing iron armor slowly walked out, with giant crossbows mounted on the elephants' backs.
"Iron-armored war elephants, they actually used the Imperial Guards!" Some soldiers shouted in horror.
Fang Zhentian's expression changed drastically, knowing that a complete defeat was inevitable. Iron-armored war elephants are the symbol of the barbarian royal court, and their appearance means that the barbarians have tried their best.
"Father, take Yunting away, and I'll take the throne!" Fang Wenyuan suddenly calmed down, a look of determination flashed in his eyes.
He took off a bronze tiger charm from his chest and stuffed it into Fang Zhentian's hand, "Give this to my mother and tell her that my son is unfilial and can no longer serve her."
"Wenyuan, no!" Just as Fang Zhentian was about to stop him, Fang Wenyuan had already turned his horse's head and raised his sword high.
"Zhenbei Army, charge with me!"
Like a flashback, the remaining soldiers followed Fang Wenyuan and rushed towards the iron wall composed of armored war elephants.
Fang Wenyuan took the lead, his sword shining in the sun, and his figure looked particularly lonely and heroic in the charge.
"Second uncle!" Fang Yunting cried bitterly and wanted to pursue him immediately, but was held tightly by Fang Zhentian.
"Let's go! Don't let their battle and death be in vain!" Fang Zhentian burst into tears, holding back his grief and pulling him back.
However, it seemed that it was too late. The barbarian cavalry had already surrounded them from both sides, cutting off all retreat routes. The armored war elephants breathed out fierce flames, trapping the remaining Zhenbei Army in the sea of ​​fire.
Fang Zhentian knew there was no hope of escape, so he straightened up his spear. Fang Yunting smiled miserably: "Child, are you afraid?"
